source_evidence: Consider the size of your investment, how long you expect to own the mutual fund and your need to access the money you invested when you think of the trade-off between share classes that charge front-end sales loads, CDSLs, and ongoing fees.
answer: When comparing share classes of the same mutual fund, consider both how much you plan to invest and how long you expect to hold the shares. These factors matter because classes can charge different combinations of upfront sales loads, fees when shares are redeemed (CDSLs), and ongoing fees. Also consider when you might need access to your money. A class with a lower initial charge may not have the lowest costs over your entire holding period, so compare the fees over the time you expect to invest.
